name: Continuous Manufacturing and Advanced Control
blurb: Where AI fits in continuous processes.
title: Continuous Manufacturing and Advanced Control
answer: Continuous manufacturing runs material through without stopping between steps, which depends on real time monitoring and control, a natural place for AI models. ICH Q13 sets the international expectations for continuous manufacturing of drug substances and products.

reading.body:
ICH Q13, adopted in November 2022, sets the international expectations for continuous manufacturing of drug substances and products, and AI control models used in those processes become part of the control strategy that must be described in the filing.

Continuous manufacturing runs material through without stopping between steps. That removes the batch boundaries where quality was traditionally checked, so control has to happen in real time on the line. Real time monitoring and control is the kind of problem models fit, which is why continuous processes are a natural place for AI in drug manufacturing.

The regulatory consequence is the part that matters. An AI model in this setting is not a side tool. It is part of the control strategy, and the filing has to describe it. That puts model behavior inside the same documented, reviewed framework as the rest of the process, which shapes how such models are built and maintained.

The data covers one guideline and one principle. It does not say which companies run continuous lines, how many have filed, what the models predict, or how regulators have responded to specific submissions. It also does not connect this to compute, buildings, or power, and nothing here supports drawing that link.

explainer:
Batch manufacturing makes a product in discrete lots, with material held between steps for testing. Continuous manufacturing feeds raw materials in and product out without stopping, which can shrink equipment, cut cycle times and improve consistency. It depends on real time monitoring, often through process analytical technology, and on control systems that keep the process in its target state.

AI fits here as soft sensors that estimate quality attributes from process data, as models that detect disturbances and divert nonconforming material, and as advanced controllers. ICH Q13 sets international expectations for continuous manufacturing, including how to define batches, control strategy and material traceability. Because control models become part of the control strategy, they must be described in the regulatory filing and validated accordingly.
